positions.title: Do the checks survive the opponent's queen? — Pa2
positions.prompt: Qd8+ initiates a checking sequence, but the defending queen has counterchecks and queen-capture resources. A single promising check does not establish perpetual repetition. Study-specific context: White's a-pawn remains if queens exchange; it changes the later material verdict. Independently calculate the defender's reply and five complete plies.
positions.replyReason: Black can answer a quiet Qd5 with ...Qe3+ or punish Qh4? with ...Qxh4; the white king must answer any resulting check. Material context: White's a-pawn remains if queens exchange; it changes the later material verdict
positions.continuationReason: At the endpoint: Kh1 preserves the queen in the first branch, while Qh4 loses the queen to ...Qxh4. Exact perpetual-check draw conditions have not been demonstrated.
